name: SEOmedSEB Smart Search for WooCommerce
author: SEOmedSEB

sections.description:
SEOmedSEB Smart Search for WooCommerce is a fast, self-hosted AJAX search plugin for WooCommerce stores, focused on two things:

  1. Deep, code-free design customization. The Design tab exposes colors, typography, spacing, border radius, and several built-in style presets (minimal, command palette, glassmorphism, sharp, rounded) as CSS variables, with a live preview.
  2. A relevance engine with typo tolerance built in. Search runs against a dedicated, optimized index table (not the slow default WordPress search), with fuzzy/SOUNDEX fallback matching so misspelled searches still find the right product.

Every feature in this plugin — including the search engine, the full Design tab, analytics, and the indexer — is free. There is no “Pro” upsell built into this version.

Key features

  • Custom, optimized search index (own DB table, not wp_posts LIKE queries)
  • AJAX autocomplete with grouped results: products, categories, tags, posts, pages
  • Product detail panel on hover — add to cart without leaving the search results
  • Typo-tolerant search (fuzzy/SOUNDEX fallback + “did you mean” suggestions)
  • Synonyms, and exclude/include filter rules by category, tag, or product
  • Full search-scope control (description, short description, SKU, attributes, categories, tags, custom fields)
  • Deep design customization: colors, typography, spacing, radius, style presets, dark mode
  • Animated (“typewriter”) placeholder with a configurable phrase list and speed
  • ⌘K / Ctrl+K global search shortcut
  • Mobile overlay mode with configurable breakpoint
  • Client-side “recent searches” history
  • Search analytics: critical (zero-result) search phrases report + dashboard widget
  • Scheduled + on-demand index rebuilding, with live progress in the admin

Adding the search bar to your theme

  1. Shortcode: [smart_search_bar]
  2. Widget: Appearance → Widgets → “Smart Search bar”
  3. PHP: <?php echo do_shortcode( '[smart_search_bar]' ); ?>
sections.installation:
1. Upload the seomedseb-smart-search folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the zip via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin. WooCommerce must already be installed and active.
  3. The plugin will automatically build its search index in the background. Check progress under WooCommerce → Smart Search → Indexer.
  4. Add [smart_search_bar] wherever you want the search bar to appear, or use the widget.
sections.faq:
Does this require WooCommerce?

Yes, WooCommerce must be installed and active.

Is this really free?

Yes. Every feature described above is included at no cost. A future paid tier may exist someday, but it is a separate, later decision and does not affect this version.

Does it work with variable products?

Yes, and you choose how. Under Search config → Product variations you can show only the parent product (variation SKUs still match it), give each variation its own result row with its own price, stock and image, or list the matching variations underneath their parent.
sections.changelog:
0.18.33

  • Fixed: a product mentioning a search word many times in its description could outrank the product whose title matches the search exactly (“trangia 25-2” showing a 25-21 first). The database score now only breaks ties.
  • Improved: the plugin now loads minified copies of its own JavaScript and CSS (about half the size), as flagged by PageSpeed Insights. The readable source files are still included, and are loaded instead when SCRIPT_DEBUG is on.

0.18.32

  • Added: spelling correction. When a search finds nothing, misspelled words are corrected against the words used in your product titles (“trangai” → “trangia”, “tasmanain tiger” → “tasmanian tiger”) and the corrected results are shown straight away, with a “Showing results for …” note (editable under Texts). Model numbers are never “corrected”.
  • Fixed: “templars gear” didn’t find “Templar’s Gear”, and “miltec” barely found “Mil-Tec”. Names with apostrophes or hyphens are now also indexed without them (a reindex runs automatically after updating).
  • Fixed: “Rebuild index” emptied the search index before rebuilding it, so the live search found next to nothing for the minute or two the rebuild took. Rows are now overwritten in place and only products that no longer exist are removed at the end — this also cleans deleted products out of the nightly reindex.
  • Fixed: searches containing an apostrophe (“templar’s gear”) could be blocked by the web server’s firewall with a 403, leaving the dropdown empty. Apostrophes are no longer sent with the search.
  • Fixed: with a full-page cache (NitroPack, WP Rocket, Cloudflare…) serving pages older than WordPress’s 12–24 hour nonce lifetime, every search from those pages was rejected and the dropdown stayed empty. The search now fetches a fresh nonce and retries automatically.
  • Fixed: a search containing a common English word such as “the”, “for” or “with” (“ticket to the moon carabiner”) found nothing, because MySQL never indexes those words and a required one empties the result. They are now ignored.
  • Improved: compound words — “sovepose til børn” now finds a “Børnesovepose” (Danish, German and Swedish write these as one word, and FULLTEXT only matches the start of a word). Filler words like “til”, “og” and “the” no longer count towards ranking.
  • Improved: an exact model number in the title now outweighs a partial brand match, so “trangia 25-2” ranks “Trangiakök 25-2 UL” above “Trangia 25-21”. When a mixed search like “G&G karabiner” has no product matching every word, products matching either part are ranked together instead of dropping the brand.

0.18.31

  • Fixed: searches with short model numbers or codes found the wrong products — “trangia 25-2” showed a 250 ml Trangia mug instead of the 25-2 storm cooker. MySQL’s FULLTEXT index skips words shorter than 3 characters (“25”, “2”, “UL”), so these were dropped or prefix-matched longer words like “250”. Such words are now required as written and results are ranked word by word: an exact “25-2” in the title comes first, “25-21” next, unrelated products not at all.

0.18.30

  • Fixed: names containing “&” (e.g. the brand “G&G Armament”) showed as “G&G” in the dropdown, and searching “G&G” found nothing. WordPress stores “&” as “&” in term names and some product titles; the index now stores plain text, category/brand/tag search matches the stored form, and “G&G” is no longer ignored when combined with other words (“G&G karabiner” now only finds G&G products). Updating rebuilds the index automatically.

0.18.29

  • Changed: with “All variation SKUs” display, a product with many variations no longer lists every code. The results list shows the first 3 and the details panel the first 6, followed by “+N more”; codes matching the search come first, so a searched variant SKU is always visible and highlighted. The “+N more” text can be edited under Texts.

0.18.28

  • Fixed: variable products with many variations could be missing from search entirely — not findable by name or by any variation SKU. A product’s index row holds every variation’s SKU, and with many variations that passed the 191-character limit of the SKU column, so the row was never saved. The column is now TEXT; updating converts it automatically and rebuilds the index.

Earlier versions

The full changelog back to the 0.1.0 initial release (0.18.27 through 0.1.0) is kept in changelog-full.txt in the plugin’s own folder, and in the version history on this plugin’s SVN repository — trimmed here so this section stays under WordPress.org’s 5000-character display limit for the Changelog tab.
